gap: No result ChatGPT got states the named measured AC output of the under-$200 candidates side by side: StorageReview got 210 Wh out of the EcoFlow RIVER 3's rated 245 Wh (270 Wh from the wall to refill) and The Solar Lab got 45 minutes at 273 W (about 83%), while no named reviewer has published a measured usable-capacity figure for the BLUETTI Elite 30 mini.
standout_why: Neither cited page has a measured figure: The Inertia (cited, 2025-12-10) gives only the RIVER 3's 245 Wh rating and a one-hour charge, and PowerSized (cited, 2026-11-27) gives only $199 / 288 Wh / 300 W / 7.3 lb for the Elite 30 mini. Watt & Warden, MachineFanatic, RadarOfProducts and RV Gear Lab state they did not test and carry maker specs only. The Power Station Guide (rank 12, not cited) already has part of it: The Solar Lab's RIVER 3 recharge times (58 min warm, 1 h 20 cold), a 'PortablePowerNerd measured ~240–245Wh usable' line that StorageReview's 210 Wh contradicts, and Outdoor Gear Lab's 60–93% range. None has StorageReview's 210 Wh / 270 Wh, Outdoor Gear Lab's per-model figures, or a side-by-side. Yahoo's under-$250 page returned 403 and was not compared.
decides: It does not decide the pick. The RIVER 3 is the only candidate with two named measurements (about 205–210 Wh usable, 84–86% of rated), which supports ChatGPT's 'roughly four hours at 50 W' (210 Wh / 50 W = 4.2 h). The Elite 30 mini's 288 Wh rating has no named measurement behind it, so the page can only state the rated figure and say so. The two 300 Wh-class units Outdoor Gear Lab measured (Anker SOLIX C300 230 Wh, Jackery Explorer 300 260 Wh) are $329.99 and $289 on Amazon today, so they fall outside the line. The Elite 30 mini stays in the line at $199 on rated capacity, weight and price, not on a measured figure.
